storyline.label: On-Policy Distillation
storyline.latest_title: Agentic-OPD: Recovering Forgotten Agent Capabilities via On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Tasks

prior_narrative.tldr: Papers from Oct 14 apply on-policy distillation (training a student on its own sampled trajectories, scored by a teacher) to translation and long-horizon coding agents. By Oct 22 the work turned to when the student should follow the teacher, and by Oct 26 to multi-agent serving configuration.
prior_narrative.whats_new: Oct 30: DecisionRank, an arXiv paper, applies on-policy distillation to transfer a generative LLM's ranking knowledge into a decision model that predicts scores directly, avoiding autoregressive decoding latency.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: On-policy distillation is spreading from post-training into serving components such as multi-agent routing and rerankers, so teams can test it on latency- and cost-sensitive parts of a stack, not only on small chat models.
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: If you run an LLM reranker or router, benchmark a distilled decision model against it on your own queries for quality and latency before switching; none of these papers has independent replication yet.

beats.headline: Qwen-MT-Lumen applies on-policy training to WMT 2026 translation
OPRD distills constraint reminders into long-horizon coding agents
Advantage-based method decides when to follow the teacher
EvoRouter applies on-policy distillation to multi-agent routing cost
DecisionRank distills LLM ranking knowledge into a decision-model reranker

open_questions: Does the advantage-based method beat plain on-policy distillation on agentic coding tasks, not only its own benchmarks?
Does any group release code that reproduces the OPRD long-horizon results?
Do EvoRouter's cost savings hold on production query mixes outside its own benchmark?
Does DecisionRank's distilled reranker match its LLM teacher's ranking quality on a third party's data?
